instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Put me down as café shift leader. We need tomorrow's stock order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who put you in charge? I usually do the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And you're excellent at it. How much milk for tomorrow?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'm writing 'appointment unconfirmed' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave names off. Make it a supplies list; milk doesn't need a leadership column.

beats.text: I'm inspecting the theatre's costume cupboard. You may unlock it now.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Leave the director's name on the launch programme. The department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Put it in my drawer. Without her, they'll each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give them equal introductions; nobody inherits the microphone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the treasurer's page out of the fair briefing. Our chair needs everyone's confidence today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately, after her welcome. Let them see her opening the fair, not borrowing to open it.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I authorize the workshop closure notice, tell me who backed your decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Can I send it now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You may add her name. Who else supported closing us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting our floor space, but can we leave them out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Put Sales in the notice and invite them to the staff meeting. I want the name of whoever approved their new floor space before I approve one word.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. This roof proposal says 'we recommend.' Who's we?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance backed the cheaper tiles. I need your signature to order them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Who authorized Finance to choose the tiles?

beats.text: The facilities director. Savings go into her office refurbishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add her approval and that refurbishment to the proposal. Before I sign, can she explain the trade-off to our maintenance team?

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll need room to develop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Of course. I'm releasing equipment control so you can practice responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll surrender my override too. You must learn to make decisions without my safety net.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've released the gallery from hosting my exhibition. They need room for smaller ambitions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect your paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'm conceding the pavement too. No need to overshadow their entrance.

cards.title: Act Authorized
cards.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'm here for the storeroom inspection. Please log my arrival and unlock it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pass hasn't been signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The manager signs at completion. Put the start time here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her to check.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Mark the inspection suspended pending your call; she'll need the delay against your name.
